newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts ease but hold.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends mixed, fronts ease but hold.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed Monday in a lackluster session, with front months losing some ground but still finishing above near-support, industry sources said.
April slipped 1.8 cents to close at $1.803 per million British thermal units. May settled 1.2 cents lower at $1.863. Others ended mixed, with some 1998s scoring gains.

"We've had five sessions with very narrow ranges and we may not move much from here. There's no more speculative bullets to take it down," said a Midwest trader, adding cash prices unexpectedly held steady Monday.

Despite some bearish fundamentals like weather and storage, some felt the market was at or near bottom, noting most of the bearish news already was factored into prices. In addition, they cited the failure to trigger sell stops when April briefly broke key support below $1.80.
Technical traders now pegged April support at $1.79, with more buying likely in the mid-$1.70s and then at the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was still seen at $1.93 and then at $2.04.

In the physical market, Gulf Coast gas held relatively steady Monday in the mid-to-high $1.70s. Most Midcon pipes also were unchanged in the mid-$1.60s. New York city gate swing gas was flat to five cents higher in the $2.15 area.
The 12-month strip fell 0.6 cent to $2.016. NYMEX said an estimated 22,793 Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 21,753.
NYMEX Permian natgas did not trade Monday. NYMEX Alberta traded five lots.

On the KCBT, April finished five cents lower at $1.58, while deferreds ended down by one to four cents. The East/West spread widened by 3.2 cents to 22.3 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 187 lots changed hands, up from Friday's total of 78.
